findings.title: Default `queued` timestamp is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated when the class is defined, so every AssignmentSource that doesn't pass `queued` gets the same process-start timestamp. The field is meant to record when the assignment was queued. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: to_dict output contains a datetime that is not JSON serializable
findings.body: `asdict(self)` returns `queued` as a datetime. The dict is passed as a kwarg to `apply_async` in `sync_group_assignee_outbound`. Celery with the JSON serializer will fail or convert it to a string. On deserialization `from_dict` then passes `queued` as a str, which is never validated. Serialize the datetime explicitly (isoformat) and parse it back, or drop the field.

findings.title: assignment_source kwarg passed to all integrations' sync_assignee_outbound
findings.body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`. The abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` accepts `**kwargs`, but concrete implementations (Jira, VSTS, GitHub, etc.) are not updated here. Any implementation without `**kwargs` will raise a TypeError. The diff does not show that these were checked.

findings.title: Inbound sync paths are not tested for passing an assignment source
findings.body: The tests verify the outbound skip when `assignment_source` is passed directly to `assign`. They do not check that `sync_group_assignee_inbound` actually passes `AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)`. There is also no test for deassign with a matching source, or for the task-level dict round trip. A regression in the cycle-breaking wiring would go unnoticed.
